Thanks again for the demo last week. We started ramping steady traffic to the reserved pool over the last two days and saw intermittent tail latency spikes during your documented peak hours (roughly 10:30-11:15 PT). Attaching a small sample of logs + request traces.

High level:
- 95th percentile is acceptable; 99.9th jumps to ~2.3s for short chat responses (our target is 700ms).
- This looks tied to queueing/backpressure rather than model compute.

Can Redwood commit to a carveout or exception to the standard dedicated SLA that provides a tighter queueing behavior guarantee during our peak (we're buying 40 reserved GPUs)? If you need, we can share a small replay dataset.

Connor and I are looping in procurement next week; a written note on expected headroom and monitoring we'd get would help.

1) I’ll pull in engineering to validate the traces and reproduce with a replay on a staging reserved pool.

I’ll loop in Vivek (ops) and Marissa (account) to run through feasibility and any precedent.

Thanks for the trace, Maya — good reproduction candidates. Quick engineering read and proposal: 

Findings (from staging replay):
- The spike pattern matches an inflight headroom exhaustion under sustained small-batch chat load. When headroom hits zero, requests are queued into a best-effort path which can add ~1.2–1.6s depending on backlog.
- We do offer tenant-priority lanes for reserved pools. By default, the lane provides best-effort fallback behavior when the pool is saturated.

Proposal for a PivotalAI carveout/trial:
1) Trial (2 weeks) on a dedicated staging slice configured with:
   - Tenant-priority lane with an elevated inflight headroom (configured to Pivotal’s peak QPS).
   - Sticky KV caching enabled for short-chats to lower tail tokens.
2) Measured SLA targets during peak window (10:00–12:00 PT):
   - 99.9th < 800ms for the primary conversation workload (as defined by replay).
   - 95th < 350ms.
3) Observability: shared Grafana dashboard + daily automated trace export (token-level samples) during trial.
4) If trial misses target on >2 non-consecutive days, we offer a one-time credit equal to 10% of that month’s reserved capacity fee and a remediation runbook.
5) For long-term contract: include a queueing stability addendum that codifies config knobs (headroom levels, burst tokens), monitoring access, and remediation credits.

Caveats: this treatment costs some operational capacity (we allocate a prioritized headroom in the pool), so full long-term support likely requires an uplift in reserved commit (we should call this out in the commercial).

If everyone is aligned I’ll get infra/ops to spin the trial cluster and produce a short technical addendum for legal/commercial review.

—Vivek
